newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DOCDATA SEES BIG ACQUISITION THIS YEAR.
newsitem.headline: DOCDATA SEES BIG ACQUISITION THIS YEAR.

text.p: Dutch compact disc maker DOCdata said on Wednesday it expected to announce a substantial acquisition before the end of 1997.
"We plan an acquisition before the end of this year and this should add 20 to 30 percent to our annual turnover," chairman Hans van Gerwen said in an interview.

The group's turnover rose to 62.8 million guilders during the first six months of 1997 compared to 52.5 million during the same period of 1996, DOCdata reported earlier today. Net sales were 115.5 million guilders during the whole of 1996.
Earlier today DOCdata reported a growth in net profits of just over 60 percent during the first six months of 1997 to 4.3 million guilders.
Van Gerwen, who sees organic growth of between 20 to 25 percent in the next three years, said DOCdata aims to expand through acquisition in several areas.
He mentioned the CD-ROM segment including distribution as well as moving in to regions in Europe where it had no presence.
"We think of Britain, Scandinavia or countries in the south of Europe, like Spain, Portugal or Italy," he said.
Another area where expansion was under consideration was in the field of duplicators in Europe and the United States, he said.
"We have 65 million guilders available for acquisitions," financial officer Jaap Ruigrok said, part in cash.
Van Gerwen added DOCdata had sought a listing in Amsterdam and on NASDAQ earlier this year to finance future growth.
The firm said it did not yet aim for expansion in Eastern Europe and Asia as rights are not yet patented in those areas.
